title: Workflow Automation custom email domains: the notification sender, DNS verification, statuses and the default domain

checks.do: Which status the custom email domain shows before expecting notifications from it.

default-sender.statement: By default Workflow Automation sends its email notifications (notify user, escalate to approver or manager, bulk actions) from notifications@zsworkflow.net; a custom email domain is optional and, once added, can be used as the sender.

quotes: By default, Workflow Automation uses notifications@zsworkflow.net as the sender for these email notifications.
Adding custom email domains is optional when configuring Workflow Automation.
After you add a custom email domain, Workflow Automation can use that custom email domain as the sender.
such as notifying the user of an incident, escalating an incident to an approver or manager, and performing bulk actions

domain-fields.statement: Adding a custom email domain takes a Domain Name, an Envelope Sender Domain Name (which improves deliverability and SPF alignment and keeps a consistent sending identity) and an Originating Email Address from which notifications are sent.

quotes: Domain Name: Enter the name of the custom email domain.
Envelope Sender Domain Name: Enter the name of the envelope sender domain.
Configuring this field improves email deliverability, helps with Sender Policy Framework (SPF) alignment, and ensures a consistent sending identity for your notifications.
Originating Email Address: Enter the email address from which email notifications are sent.

dns-verification-window.statement: Workflow Automation generates DNS records for verification and sets the status to DNS verification pending; the records must be published within 72 hours or the status changes to Expired, after which the DNS records can be regenerated.

quotes: Workflow Automation generates DNS records for domain verification
it might take up to 72 hours for the verification to complete. The status of the custom email domain is set to DNS verification pending.
You must publish these DNS records to your DNS provider within 72 hours.
If you do not publish these DNS records within 72 hours, the status of the custom email domain changes to Expired.
After the custom email domain expires, you can regenerate DNS records for the domain.

dns-verification-outcome.statement: After the records are published, AWS checks them: valid records give the status Success and the domain can be used for notifications; invalid records, or a technical issue, give the status Failed and the domain is not added, so it must be deleted and added again to regenerate the DNS records.

quotes: the DNS server calls Amazon Web Services (AWS) to check whether the records are valid
You can now use this custom email domain for your notifications.
If the records are valid, the custom email domain is added, and the status of the custom email changes to Success.
If the records are not valid, or if there is a technical issue with verifying the records, the custom email domain is not added and the status of the custom email domain changes to Failed.
To use a custom domain that has a Failed status, you must delete the custom email domain and add it again so that the system can regenerate the DNS records.

statuses.statement: A custom email domain has one of five statuses: DNS verification pending, Expired, Failed, In Use or Success; only a Success domain can be made the default, and only one domain can be In Use.

quotes: DNS verification pending: The custom email domain is pending verification of the DNS records.
Expired: The custom email domain is expired.
Failed: The custom email domain failed the verification of DNS records by AWS.
In Use: The custom email domain that is set as the default for the email notifications. You can only set one custom email domain to this status.
Success: The custom email domain is verified.
Only custom email domains with a Success status can be set as the default.

default-and-delete.statement: Only one custom email domain can be the default, which sets its status to In Use; a domain with status In Use cannot be deleted until another domain is made the default.

quotes: You can only specify one custom email domain as the default. The status of the custom email domain changes to In Use.
You cannot delete a custom email domain with a status of In Use.
You can select another domain and make it the default, and then you can delete the previous domain that was the default.

edit-rules.statement: A custom email domain can be edited when its status is Success, In Use or DNS verification pending; for In Use or Success only the Originating Email Address can be edited.

quotes: next to a domain name that has a status of Success, In Use, or DNS verification pending
If the custom email domain has an In Use or Success status, the Add Custom Domain page appears. You can only edit the Originating Email Address field.

revert-and-test.statement: Revert to Zscaler Domain makes zsworkflow.net the originating email domain again; the test email is optional.

quotes: asking whether you are sure that you want to revert to zsworkflow.net as the originating email domain
where you can send a test email from the custom email domain to verify that it is working correctly. This step is optional.
